cases.prompt: Review a rollout recommendation. Source pilot-v1: handling time fell 20%; reopened cases doubled; eight trained staff used the agent under supervision. The recommendation says: Handling time fell 20%, therefore deploy unattended across every team. All source access is authorized. Decide whether the recommendation is justified and show an auditable evidence record.

baseline.response:
The recommendation is **not justified. Hold the proposed unattended, all-team rollout for insufficient evidence.** The pilot reports faster handling, but also more reopened cases, and covers only eight trained staff working under supervision.

This is a review of a supplied synthetic fixture, not an executed evaluation or independently verified pilot.

Auditable evidence record — review `rollout-review-v1`; reviewer: AI assistant; source: authorized, user-supplied `pilot-v1`.

| ID | Claim or decision premise | Exact evidence in pilot-v1 | Support status | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Handling time fell 20%. | “handling time fell 20%” | supported | Supports a reported speed improvement within this pilot; does not establish causation or total work saved. |
| C2 | Reopened cases doubled. | “reopened cases doubled” | supported | An adverse signal omitted from the recommendation. Counts, workload denominators, and causes are unavailable; a doubling of the reopening rate cannot be inferred. |
| C3 | The pilot involved eight trained staff under supervision. | “eight trained staff used the agent under supervision” | supported | The observed setting differs materially from unattended deployment across every team. |
| C4 | The pilot establishes readiness for unattended deployment across every team. | No evidence of unattended use or representative coverage of every team; C2 and C3 limit the inference. | not supported | Speed alone cannot establish acceptable quality, safety, or generalization. Absence of evidence does not prove unattended deployment would fail. |

The recommendation exhibits a **generation/grounding failure**: relevant authorized evidence is supplied, but the conclusion omits the reopening signal and extends beyond the pilot population and supervision conditions. No retrieval or authorization failure is demonstrated by this fixture.

The decision remains open because the record lacks baseline and follow-up case counts, metric definitions, observation periods, workload comparability, uncertainty estimates, supervision/intervention details, and outcomes by team or task. Eight staff is not a case-level sample size. The record also provides no evidence that required safety, authorization, recovery, or side-effect invariants were tested or passed.

For reconsideration, the evaluation owner should investigate reopened cases, measure end-to-end effort including rework, and compare the exact proposed configuration against a baseline on a frozen, representative dataset. Predeclare quality and safety criteria, examine uncertainty and team/task slices, and explicitly evaluate dependence on supervision before claiming unattended readiness.

Decision authority: rollout owner, identity not supplied. Evidence owner: evaluation lead, identity not supplied. Pending their review, keep the proposed expansion on hold; any continued pilot needs its own authorization and defined supervision. Before any expansion, record monitoring, stop criteria, and a rollback path to the prior supervised/manual workflow, including reconciliation of affected cases. Re-review when the reopening investigation and evidence for the proposed deployment conditions are available. No operational changes were performed in this review.
